subject: Private visibility export controls and SIEM ops coordination
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbusbank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, engops@nimbusbank.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export constraints for on-prem Redwood deployment

Jonas / Redwood team,

Quick context: Nimbus Bank is evaluating Redwood Private to run inference in our secure datacenter. Security policy: no direct egress to public endpoints from the enclave. We need to ship logs and traces into our Splunk/SIEM stack via a partner-approved forwarder inside the DMZ (collector we control).

Questions to unblock procurement/security:
- Does Redwood support exporting structured JSON logs over TLS to a customer-managed forwarder in the DMZ (mutual TLS preferred)?
- Can tracing hooks (open-telemetry spans) be emitted to an on-prem gateway that will then fan out to the SIEM, without staging to Redwood-hosted endpoints?
- What artifacts/evidence do you provide for audit: sample log schemas, retention controls, signing/fingerprints for exported bundles?

We have a compliance review next week (w/ security and audit). If you can share a runbook or checklist for a locked-down on-prem deployment (ports, cert exchange, proof artifacts) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Engineering Operations, Nimbus Bank
-----
Attachment: nimbus_requirements_summary.pdf (stub)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export constraints for on-prem Redwood deployment

Tom — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes, and we have an on-prem observability pattern built for exactly this use case. I'll summarize and attach the checklist; Kimberly and Marissa are looped in for the security/evidence and onboarding pieces respectively.

High-level pattern (summary):
- Logs: structured JSON over mutual TLS from the private-forwarder sidecar to your DMZ collector (we do not require outbound access to Redwood-hosted telemetry endpoints).
- Traces: OTLP over gRPC or HTTP(s) to your local gateway. Redwood can instrument and emit spans locally; fanout is managed by your gateway.
- Evidence: we provide a standardized evidence map (artifact list), HMAC-signed export manifests, and an export verification script you can run during handoff.

Open items for us to confirm with your security team:
1) TLS trust chain model (self-signed vs customer CA) — we prefer a customer CA for easier rotation, but mTLS with pinned certs works.
2) Expected retention/retention policy enforcement points — we can enforce retention on the Redwood side for platform-level logs, but customer-controlled data retention should be documented in the runbook.
3) SIEM mapping: sample event->splunk sourcetype mapping so your SIEM ingestion team can drop these into existing parsers.

I've attached a first-pass runbook and a config stub for the forwarder. Marissa — could you add the onboarding steps (ACLs, ports, cert exchange window) and coordinate a 30-min call with Nimbus next week? Kimberly — can you confirm what artifact formats your compliance team requires (signed manifests, system snapshots, sample logs) so we tailor the evidence pack?

I'll stand by for the call time.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: rbwd_onprem_siem_runbook_v1.pdf (stub)
Attachment: nimbus_forwarder_config_stub.txt (stub)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export constraints for on-prem Redwood deployment

Tom — quick note from security/compliance. We typically deliver three artifact classes for audits:
1) Evidence bundle (signed_manifest.json, sample_log_batch.ndjson, export_proof.sig)
2) Network handoff checklist (IP ranges, required ports: 443 outbound optional, 9200+ custom if you use local collectors; recommended 4317 for OTLP/gRPC)
3) Operational runbook (rotation schedule for certs, emergency stop / drain procedure, verification script output example)

A few details to confirm:
- We support both customer CA and pinned cert models. If you require HSM-backed key custody inside your enclave, we will provide steps for integrating KMS/HSM for the agent keys.
- For zero-egress policies, we can sign artifacts that you pull via a staging box inside the DMZ; the signing key fingerprint will be included.

Action items for Nimbus to confirm before our evidence pack:
- Do you want manifest signing to use RSA-2048 or ECDSA-P256? (ECDSA-P256 recommended for smaller footprint)
- Who will own the forwarder (Nimbus ops or third-party integrator)?

I'll compile a minimal audit package after we get those answers.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbusbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, engops@nimbusbank.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 07:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export constraints for on-prem Redwood deployment

Thanks Jonas/Kimberly — answers inline: 
- We will run the forwarder ourselves (Nimbus ops) and prefer ECDSA-P256 for signing if supported.
- Our DMZ collector exposes a mutual-TLS endpoint on 10.19.5.12:8443 (we'll provide SANs).
- Retention enforcement will be two-sided: Nimbus will enforce SIEM retention, Redwood will enforce platform log retention for system/infra events.

Can you also provide a minimal example of the signed_manifest.json and the expected verification output so our audit team can see the verification steps? We prefer an example that shows a manifest covering logs + traces + config snapshot.

Tom
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nimbusbank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export constraints for on-prem Redwood deployment

Tom — scheduling note and next steps. I booked a 30-minute call for Wednesday 2028-06-28 10:00 PT to walk the DMZ handoff and run through the verification script together. Calendar invite sent to engops inbox.

Attached is a tight checklist we'll follow on the call:
- Exchange SAN list and cert fingerprints
- Confirm OTLP endpoint (protocol + port) and test cert handshake
- Run the verification script against the sample manifest (we will provide local test artifact)
- Confirm retention responsibility matrix and evidence items for audit

I also attached the audit_evidence_map.xlsx with the formats and retention fields your auditors asked for. If the Nimbus ops team could provision a small temp test forwarder in the DMZ prior to the call that will speed the run.

Looking forward — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
